h: Vayetzei Ois 3 · Shabbat Contains the Festivals and the Blessing of All Days
Shabbat Contains the Festivals: Pesach and Redemption

p: In the Maariv prayer of Shabbat
we say, "You blessed it above all the days
and sanctified it above all the seasons."
means the holiness of the three pilgrimage festivals,
for included within the holiness of Shabbat
That is: the holiness of the festival of Pesach
is the matter of the redemption from Egypt,
and it is found in the root of Shabbat's holiness,
two Shabbatot according to their laws,
And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21) it is stated:
"And because of this the early ones said:
one Shabbat according to its law,
Now "the early ones said" truly alludes
to the Gemara's exposition cited above,
for it is truly one matter:
also as referring to one Shabbat,
which is called by the term "My Shabbatot."
As they expounded from what is said,
the intent being the two holinesses
of the Upper Shabbat and the Lower Shabbat.
And as is stated in the holy Zohar
on the verse "My Shabbatot you shall keep":
that is, the Upper Heh and the Lower Heh.

h: Upper and Lower Fear; the Yoke of Torah

p: is the aspect of the revelation of the Kingship of Heaven
and from this fear [of Heaven] shines forth
And as is stated at the beginning of Orach Chaim:
that when one takes to heart
that the King of kings stands over him,
there will immediately come to him
And this fear resides in the heart,
עַל פָּסוּק לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֶב אָיִן
on the verse "to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart" —
[said] concerning those who engage in Torah
but have no fear of Heaven,
which is called by the name "heart."
And the Upper Heh is "Binah is the heart,"
meaning when the fear has already been acquired
in the innermost point of the heart.
to fear in the outer dimension;
and about this our Sages of blessed memory said
"The awe of Shabbat is upon the unlearned" —
which is the aspect of fear
in the outer part of the heart.
This is along the lines of their saying
"Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah,
the yoke of worldly occupation is removed from him."
יָפֶה תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
"Torah study is good together with a worldly occupation,
for the toil of both makes sin forgotten" —
so it appears that one needs
the yoke of worldly occupation together with the Torah.
However, this is only after the corruption
"By the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread";
and this too was for his good,
the Lord your God chastises you."

h: Worldly Bounty and Chastening as Divine Help

p: regarding the promises of this world
they are not the reward for the mitzvot,
for in this world there is none,
and the essential reward is in the World to Come.
Rather, it is that the Blessed Name
that "if you walk in My statutes" —
הַיְינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר נְקַבֵּל עָלֵינוּ עוֹל תּוֹרָה
that is, when we accept upon ourselves the yoke of Torah —
then there will flow down upon us
all the needs of this world in abundance,
so that it not distract us
and certainly we will not be drawn
into the desire of this world,
to accept the yoke of Torah.
However, in the opposite case, Heaven forbid,
it is then necessary to chastise
with the sufferings of lacking this world's bounty;
and all this is for our good,
so that we not be drawn, Heaven forbid,
into the desire of this world.
And this is the matter as well
יְצִיר כַּפָּיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He:
"And He placed him in the Garden of Eden
to work it and to guard it" —
that is, to accept upon himself the yoke of Torah
in the positive commandments and the prohibitions
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד א)
(as is written in Zohar Part I, 27a);

he needed no toil for his livelihood.
when knowledge of the opposite entered him,

"by the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread";
and all this was for his good,
so that he not be drawn
as they of blessed memory said,

h: Remember and Keep: Shabbat Lifts the Worldly Yoke

p: Now, for Israel as a whole,
the yoke of worldly occupation is removed from them,
for they are warned not to do
any labor for the sake of livelihood.
This is because they accept the yoke of Torah
which were said in a single utterance
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כז עַמּוּד א).
to draw the holiness of Shabbat upon oneself
in actuality, from the person's side,
"'Remember' — could it mean in your heart?
the keeping of the heart is already stated;
That you repeat it with your mouth."
That is, a person should express with his mouth
in the Kiddush of the day:
with love and favor You have given us as a heritage."
for that was before the corruption,
and it was "engraved upon the Tablets" —
the words of Torah were engraved upon the heart,
and it sufficed for the soul
only to remember with the mouth
the holiness of Shabbat flowing from Above,
and it was guarded from being forgotten,
for it is "a place that has no forgetting,"
as is written in the holy Zohar.
the keeping in the heart is needed as well,
at every moment of the day of Shabbat,
lest it be forgotten from his heart;
one can come to be liable for a sin-offering,
כְּעִנְיַן פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ כּוּלֵּי
as in "the poor man stretched out his hand," etc.,
And through this keeping of Shabbat,
the souls of Israel as a whole
accept upon themselves the yoke of Torah,
and thereby there is removed from them
in the aspect of the heart's outer part,

it therefore works only for the time being;

h: Two Shabbatot and the Complete Redemption

p: And were the Children of Israel to keep
also in the innermost point of the heart,
which is the aspect of the Upper Shabbat,
then they would immediately be redeemed
כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ עוֹל תּוֹרָה בֶּאֱמֶת
For by truly accepting the yoke of Torah
down to the innermost point of the heart,
the yoke of subjugation would be removed from the soul
that is, every kind of pressure and pain
שֶׁכָּל הַגָּלִיּוֹת נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם מִצְרַיִם
For all the exiles are called by the name Mitzrayim,
(as is written in Bereshit Rabbah, parashah 16);
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה נִקְנֶה
and when the words of Torah are acquired
in the innermost point of the heart,
then the complete redemption will come
for all the souls of Israel,
for which we hope — speedily in our days.
And as is stated (in Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 20):
כָּל מִי שֶׁנּוֹתֵן דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה עַל לִבּוֹ
"Whoever sets words of Torah upon his heart,
there are nullified from him the thoughts of ..." etc.;
it enumerates eight kinds of thoughts,
and concludes: "for so it is written in the book of Tehillim:
'The precepts of the Lord are upright, gladdening the heart;
the commandment of the Lord is clear, enlightening the eyes.'"
from the eight thoughts mentioned above
alludes to when the words of Torah enter
the innermost point of the heart,
which is the aspect of "Binah is the heart,"
all eight attributes of the heart,
the Lower Heh, the heart's outer part,
up to Binah, the Upper Heh,
which is the heart's innermost part.

h: Joy of the Heart Versus Straying Thoughts

p: For of the opposite thoughts it is said:
"And you shall not stray after your heart
"'After your heart' — this is heretical thought;
'and after your eyes' — this is thought of transgression."
For the eye sees and the heart desires.
However, when words of Torah enter
joy is born in the heart,
and the eyes shine in everything,
seeing only His providence, blessed be He,
And so it is stated there,
עַל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה עַל לִבּוֹ
about one who does not set words of Torah upon his heart,
that there are given to him
"for so it is written in Mishneh Torah [Devarim]:
with joy and with gladness of heart.'"
That is, this is the essential intent:
in the innermost point of the heart;
from this joy is born in the heart,
and through this one is redeemed
that oppress and distress the soul.
And one comes to this especially
which is a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt.

p: The holiness of the festival of Shavuot as well,
the time of the Giving of the Torah,
is included in the holiness of Shabbat,
the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat.
And it is stated in Sefer HaBahir:
and set it for them in its place,
and the rest He hid away for the righteous," etc. —
meaning that on every Shabbat day
there shines forth the hidden light
[stored] for the righteous in the Time to Come,
which is a semblance of the World to Come.
is the revelation of the Oral Torah,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב.
"And God saw the light, that it was good."
And the holiness of the festival of Sukkot,
in which we say "the time of our joy"
more than in the other festivals,
in which there is also a mitzvah of joy —
the joy is born of itself,
from the revelation of the glory of His Kingship, blessed be He,
let the children of Zion exult in their King."
On the day of Shabbat too
they instituted saying, "They shall rejoice in Your Kingship";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מִצְוַת שִׂמְחָה
meaning that although it has no mitzvah of joy,
from the revelation of the glory of His Kingship, blessed be He,
and sat upon His Throne of Glory."
"'And on the day of your joy' — these are the Shabbatot";
meaning that then the joy is yours,
"My joy comes from within my fear."
And this is "They shall rejoice in Your Kingship":
in accepting the yoke of His Kingship, blessed be He,

h: Yom Kippur and Rosh Hashanah Within Shabbat

p: וְהִנֵּה גַּם קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁאָר מִקְרָאֵי קוֹדֶשׁ
Now the holiness of the other holy convocations as well
is included in the holiness of Shabbat.
For the holiness of Yom Kippur
and this is found especially on Shabbat,
that even one who worships idols like [the generation of] Enosh
מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת.
וְהַיְינוּ עוֹד בְּמַעֲלָה יוֹתֵר מִיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
This is a level even beyond Yom Kippur:
for there are four divisions of atonement,
and for one who bears a desecration of the Name,
and has no power to atone completely;
yet on Shabbat forgiveness is granted
even to one who worships idols like Enosh,
which involves desecration of the Name.
And the holiness of Rosh Hashanah too,
which is the Day of Remembrance —
"that your remembrance may rise before Me for good;
וּבַמֶּה בְּשׁוֹפָר (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז עַמּוּד א)
and through what? Through the shofar" (Rosh Hashanah 16a) —
on the day of Shabbat it is with greater eminence.
Therefore, when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat,
to raise our remembrance before Him, blessed be He, for good
through the action of the shofar,
because it is in its essence a day of remembrance,
"And God completed on the seventh day,"
and the Yerushalmi [Targum] renders: "and He desired."
creation found grace and desirability before Him
הַלְוַאי תְּהֵא מַעֲלִית חֵן לְפָנַי בְּכָל עֵת
If only you would find grace before Me at all times
just as you have found grace before Me
"Most desirable of days You called it,"
there becomes, as it were, desirable before Him
the whole creation of the six days of action,
to be remembered before Him for good.
And this is "a remembrance of the work of Creation."
And the essential intent is the souls of Israel,
for the sake of Israel, who is called "reishit."

h: Daily Blessing Through Torah and Prayer

p: Now, as to "You blessed it above all the days,"
that it is blessed more than all the days,
שֶׁנִּמְצָא בּוֹ הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁל כָּל הַיָּמִים
that the blessing of all the days is found in it:
in all the six days of action,
a blessing on the day itself,
only a blessing for the fish and for man;
which is not so on the day of Shabbat,
where a blessing is stated on the day itself,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא קז עַמּוּד ב)
in light of what is written (Bava Metzia 107b)
עַל פָּסוּק וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם
on the verse "And you shall serve the Lord your God":
"This is the reading of the Shema and prayer."
כְּאָדָם שֶׁקּוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה (בְּרָכוֹת י עַמּוּד ב)

וְעַל יְדֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שַׁחֲרִית וְעַרְבִית
and through the Shema morning and evening
one fulfills "[This Torah] shall not depart"
"He will bless your bread and your water" —
זוֹ פַּת בְּמֶלַח וְקִיתוֹן שֶׁל מַיִם.
"this is bread with salt and a jug of water."
That is, through the Torah and prayer
the food of each day is blessed;
for each day there flows down
a special blessing in a person's sustenance.
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, סב עַמּוּד א)
And as is stated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 62a)
עַל פָּסוּק וְלָקְטוּ דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ
on the verse "and they shall gather each day's portion on its day":
from one day for another day";
and in the Mechilta on this verse:

h: Every Day, Month and Shabbat Is New

p: And in the Siddur of the Rav [Shneur Zalman of Liadi],
on the verse "from one New Moon to its New Moon,"
alluding that on each Rosh Chodesh
just as of the twelve months of the year
its own permutation of the Name Havayah,
as is written in Sefer Yetzirah;
יֵשׁ בְּכָל רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת חֲדָשָׁה.
on each Rosh Chodesh there is a new renewal.
"and from one Shabbat to its Shabbat":
Therefore it is called a bride
and one is a bride only once,
during the seven days of the wedding feast —
there is a different illumination of holiness anew.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן לְשׁוֹן דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ
Likewise the expression "each day's portion on its day"
יוֹרֶה שֶׁאֵין יוֹם אֶחָד שָׁוֶה לַחֲבֵירוֹ
indicates that no day is equal to another,
also with respect to the flow of blessing;
כִּי לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
for the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create
"Who in His goodness renews each day continually
and the food of each day
as he needs on that day
And so is the plain meaning
בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ
wherever "each day's portion on its day" is said,
as in "You shall not reduce from your bricks
each day's quota on its day" —
שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין יוֹם שָׁוֶה לַחֲבֵירוֹ
which is because no day is equal to another
and according to the day's working hours
so is the tally of bricks.
And this is what is said:
"And you shall serve the Lord your God" —
to the renewal of service within the soul
the renewal of blessing flows down each day

h: Renewal of Torah and Prayer Each Day

p: For before the Giving of the Torah
the Holy One, blessed be He, would renew
each day the work of Creation
for the Holy One, blessed be He, originates a halachah
בְּכָל יוֹם בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה
each day in the Heavenly Court
(as is written in Bereshit Rabbah, parashah 49).
And after the Giving of the Torah,
the innovation of halachot was handed over
for they occupy themselves with the building of the world
in that there is found in their souls
a renewal in words of Torah,
They derived this from the word "va-avadtem" (and you shall serve),
for this is the essence of service:
that the will in the soul is renewed
As is stated on the verse
and one who has not served Him":
אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה שׁוֹנֶה פִּרְקוֹ מֵאָה פְּעָמִים
"One who reviews his chapter a hundred times is not comparable
to one who reviews his chapter a hundred and one times," etc.;
צֵא וּלְמַד מִשּׁוּק שֶׁל חַמָּרִין כּוּלֵּי
"go and learn from the donkey-drivers' market," etc.
to review one's chapter a hundred times,
[one who adds] one time beyond the habit
because his will was renewed in this.
And likewise in the service of prayer,
there is in each and every prayer,
as is stated in the writings of the Arizal,
that the refinement effected by one prayer
is not like that of another
with respect to the ascents of the worlds.

h: Shabbat Gathers and Bestows the Week's Blessing

p: And in proportion to the renewal in the soul
each day in Torah and in prayer,
in that proportion there is renewed in it
בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
on each and every one of the six days of action,
And of the day of Shabbat it is said,
and our Sages of blessed memory said (in Bereshit Rabbah):
whose omer was double on Erev Shabbat;
and it was also bread that was different
"You blessed it above all the days":
that all the flow of blessing
of the six days of action,
which flowed to the souls of Israel
according to their service in Torah and prayer,
in the holiness of the day of Shabbat.
in the Maariv prayer we say "and they shall rest on her" —
מִכָּל עֲבוֹדַת שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ.
from all the service of the six days of action that have passed.
And in the Shemoneh Esreh of Shacharit
we say "and they shall rest on him,"
meaning that the holiness of Shabbat
then bestows a flow of blessing
עַל כָּל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַבָּאִים
upon all the six days of action to come;
and this is "You blessed it above all the days."

rich.text: (Rav Tzadok) — Shabbat's holiness is fixed by God, yet each person receives it only as far as his weekday service has made him a vessel: כי קדושת השבת נמשכת כפי הכנת הקדושה בכל ימי החול כולם. It adds Hillel's ברוך ה' יום יום (Beitzah 16a), and the idea that "Remember" is needed because Shabbat, a taste of the World to Come, is easily forgotten.

rich.text: (Chassidus) — R. Aharon of Karlin reads the liturgy the same way. On Friday night we say וינוחו בה: the Shabbat of the eve, the night, the receiver. By day we say וינוחו בו: the Shabbat of the day, the giver. He ties the two to "My Shabbatot" and to the two levels of fear (lower fear, then love, then upper fear), as in paragraphs 1–2 here.
